title: G7 coordinated emergency stock release targets refined-product stress
net_new_delta: G7 leaders formally committed to a coordinated IEA release of 100 million barrels over four months, with a front-loaded substantial diesel release in the first 20 days, while pledging no energy-export restrictions among G7 members. This creates a policy-buffer state against the existing refined-product shock; it does not establish that diesel tightness is resolved.
assumptions_affected: Energy shock transmission should be modeled without an explicit emergency-policy supply buffer
Refined-product scarcity can be inferred solely from crude benchmarks
G7 export-restriction risk remains symmetric after the joint no-restrictions pledge

evidence.finding: G7 leaders committed to a coordinated IEA release of 100 million barrels beginning immediately over four months, including a front-loaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days, and pledged to refrain from energy export restrictions among G7 members.

IEA reported severe diesel-market pressure, said about 325 million barrels of the March 400-million-barrel collective action had already been released, and noted that refined-product flows remain severely constrained despite significant recovery in Middle-East crude exports.
IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said oil prices had begun falling after the reserve-release decision and that the IEA could release additional reserves if needed.

fact: The 100-million-barrel G7/IEA action is an official policy commitment, not merely a proposal.
The action is explicitly refined-product-sensitive: substantial diesel volumes are to be front-loaded within 20 days.
IEA says refined-product flows remain severely constrained even as Middle-East crude exports have recovered significantly.
model_inference: Create G7_EMERGENCY_PRODUCT_BUFFER as a time-valid policy-response state that partially offsets, but does not cancel, REFINED_PRODUCT_SUPPLY_STRESS.
Separate crude-flow recovery from diesel/refined-product scarcity and from policy-stock releases; these channels can move in opposite directions.
Do not infer normalization until actual release volumes, diesel cracks, inventories and physical product flows confirm transmission.
unknown: diesel share of the 100 million barrels
actual delivery timing and market destinations
whether further IEA releases will be required
conflicts: The policy action is large and front-loaded, but IEA simultaneously reports refined-product flows remain severely constrained; policy relief and physical scarcity coexist.
Some of the broader emergency-response accounting references prior March commitments, so the net-new physical barrels and diesel composition require implementation data.
next_decisive_check: Use the IEA's requested implementation/follow-up report due within 20 days, plus observed diesel/gasoil cracks, inventories, export flows and actual emergency-stock drawdowns, to determine whether G7_EMERGENCY_PRODUCT_BUFFER is materially relieving refined-product stress or merely slowing deterioration.

oracle.finding: A formal 100-million-barrel G7/IEA emergency release with front-loaded diesel creates a measurable policy buffer against refined-product stress; retain the underlying supply-stress state until physical inventories, cracks and flows confirm normalization.

supermesh_x.finding: Promote official G7/Elysee and IEA implementation evidence above headline price reactions; route actual stock drawdowns, diesel cracks, inventories and product flows as the decisive confirmation channels, preserving separation between policy commitment and realized supply relief.
